description:
Joe, a teenage orphan in the slums of the Doya streets, meets Danpei, a homeless, alcoholic ex-boxing coach. Danpei, seeing Joe's boxing talent, decides to train him. When Joe is sent to a terrible juvenile home for petty crimes, he meets Rikiishi who becomes his boxing rival. Danpei arrives at the home to help Joe to train in order to defeat Rikiishi. When Joe decides to seriously pursue boxing, Danpei cannot get a coaching license because of his reputation as a drunk.

(Source: AnimeNfo)

node.description:
The protagonist of the story. He is known for his long bangs and for always wearing a worn out beige coat and a red flat cap.

Not long after birth he found himself in many orphanages and facilities. However, he quickly grew tired of the boring life and frequently escaped, eventually finding his way to the Doya Town the story takes place in. Joe is rude and quick to fight, but he can also be very frivolous at times. Because of his rough upbringing he is a delinquent who likes his solitude, but he later grows to appreciate his new friends and rivals. He is not very good at understanding women, and essentially only treats them nice out of giri.

He is a bantamweight and his specialties include the cross counter and the No Guard stance. He has extraordinary punching strength, fortitude, and fighting spirit, often standing up after taking killer blows and has been known to counter cross-counters (a double-cross), possessing a raw, natural talent for the sport. He has even countered double crosses with a triple-cross, implying he has high-level technical abilities. Following his fight with [Rikiishi](https://anilist.co/character/20185/Rikiishi-Tooru), he begins to better develop his guarding.

This character page is set to represent and list all narrators, which haven't been given a visual representation of themselves in their respective work. 

Please add other narrator characters, which were given a visual representation of themselves, separately from this narrator page.

__Gym:__ Shiraki
__Weight Class:__ Welterweight
__Style(s):__ Hybrid, Brawling Style
__Stance(s):__ Orthodox Stance, Brawling Stance
__Trainer:__ [Shiraki Youko](https://anilist.co/character/46051/Shiraki-Youko) (minimal)

Rikiishi and [Joe](https://anilist.co/character/11804/Yabuki-Joe) first meet in the juvenile detention center, where Rikiishi was introduced as a boxer who was sentenced to the juvenile detention center because he had punched an member of the audience half to death after they had claimed that the match was rigged in Rikiishi's favor, enraging him.

~!On their first encounter Joe challenges Rikiishi without knowing he was once a professional boxer and manages to punch him in the face once before Rikiishi knocks him out in one punch. Thus he was quintessential in motivating Joe to start taking boxing seriously, even if his only reason is to beat Rikiishi in a rematch.!~

~!Rikiishi is widely considered to be one of the most promising rookie boxers in the world, but his career is tragically cut short, as he dies immediately after his and Joe's rematch from his injuries and the toll his extreme weight loss training took on his body.!~

Carlos Rivera is a Venezuelan bantamweight boxer who ranked #6 in the world. The reason he is called a "A King Without A Crown" is because there is a rumor that the world champion is too afraid to fight him. [Yoko Shiraki](https://anilist.co/character/46051/Shiraki-Youko) brings Rivera over to Japan to help [Joe](https://anilist.co/character/11804/Yabuki-Joe) recover.

~! After his 12-Round Match with Joe, Carlos goes to Mexico City to fight the Champion Jose Mendoza, but is knocked out in the first round, 1 minute and 33 seconds in. After the match, his manager, Robert, claims, “Carlos Rivera did not lose against the champion, Jose Mendoza. He was already broken by an unknown Japanese boxer named Joe Yabuki” confirming that Carlos was left punch drunk after his match with Joe. While offered a rematch with Jose, Robert turns it down and says that Carlos may never step into the ring ever again !~

Danpei is Joe's serious, cautious and responsible mentor who gets him started in his boxing career. He is fond of sake, being overly cheerful when drunk which contrasts with his strict everyday self. He is also very polite when talking to people who hold higher ranks than himself, something that annoys Joe, who doesn't care for such things. Before meeting Joe, it is stated that Danpei used to be a boxer himself. However, after the loss of one of his eyes, we learn that he was forced to give up on his own boxing career, aiming to become a coach instead. But due to his violent, strict, passionate, and even desperate approach to training his boxers(who couldn't take it and abandoned him for better gyms), he became jobless and eventually a homeless alcoholic.  After meeting Joe and claiming that he has massive potential for the sport, he gives up on drinking due to the former's aversion to alcoholism (only drinking on special occasions) and vows to train him to be Japan's or even the world's best boxer, with the hope of a better tomorrow for the both of them.

Yoko Shiraki is a young woman born to the Shirakis, a very wealthy family who is known for their activities in the boxing field. She is the main female protagonist in Ashita no Joe.

She is very polite, graceful and kind to other people, always acting exactly as expected from a daughter born to a family with a higher rank, donating to charities from time to time. As so, she clashes in both appearance and personality with most of the other characters who know nothing but poverty and hardship.

One of those characters is Joe who is the first to remark that her so called 'kindness' is completely fake, implying her sympathy for the poor is merely a way to make herself feel superior over those who have nothing to eat. She is often very shocked by his actions but as time goes on she comes to be the one who understands him best. She is disliked by Joe as an 'evil woman' who tries to control his life by always having something to do with most the situations he finds himself in later in the series.

~!After gradually coming to like him and showing very subtle and growing hints throughout the series, she confesses her love for Joe in the lockeroom right before the world title fight, begging him not to fight José Mendoza for her sake.!~

Nishi is Joe's best friend, sparring partner and later he also becomes Joe's trainer. He is a juvenile delinquent. He first meets Joe in a juvenile jail, where they fight each other and Joe defeats him. Nishi later meets Joe at the correction house where they become friends.

Nishi's personality changes drastically from an arrogant juvenile delinquent to calm worker at a grocery store. He takes a liking to boxing after watching Joe's match against Rikishi in the detention center.

When Joe comes back to Namida Bridge he is surprised to find Nishi at the Tange boxing gym, Nishi joins the gym to learn boxing and to continue being with Joe. Nishi is an averagely good boxer. He was the only useful sparring partner Joe had in the entire story. Nishi has a crush on Noriko Hayashi, who is the daughter of his boss at the grocery store.

~!Nishi injures his fist in a match and painfully decides to retire from boxing. In his retirement party he confesses that he will always be proud of dedicating his youth to boxing. Later, Nishi marries Noriko and becomes more dedicated to his work at the convenience store but he also continues to help Joe with his training and works in the corner during his matches.!~

A young girl from a depressed Japanese neighborhood. She idolizes [Yabuki Joe](https://anilist.co/character/11804/Yabuki-Joe) and joins him, along with a band of other kids, in committing petty crimes. She continues to believe in and support Joe throughout the story.

She is the teenage daughter of the owners of the local grocery store. She has a schoolgirl crush on Joe, which develops into romantic feelings as she matures but Joe initially does not notice her feelings and is even at times implied to be ignoring them.

~!She also disapproves of his boxing career, believing that Joe was on a suicidal path after bring consumed with guilt for inadvertently causing Rikiishi's death, in the end nothing ever happens between them. Instead, she becomes involved with, and eventually marries Nishi shortly before the end of the series, but is not shown to be especially happy with her choice.!~

He was an up-and-coming bantamweight boxer. In order to get recognition quickly, Joe targeted the bantamweight rookie champion. Wolf was a confident and brash fighter who was easily provoked by Joe into a fist fight, ending in a double knockout.
~!This news eventually led to the public demanding a match between them, which Wolf lost.!~
 
~!He eventually became a thug who got defeated due to his weak jaw, and later borrowed money from Joe after rekindling their friendship. By the end of the series he finally pays it back and supports Joe for his last match, actively cheering.!~

Mamoru Aoyama was an inmate at the juvenile detention center. Often picked on by the other inmates due to his short stature and feeble nature, he received some training from Danpei, who teaches him dodging techniques that make him a hard opponent to fight against, even managing to score a win against one of the toughest inmates during the juvie boxing tournament.
Carlos Rivera's manager & childhood bestfriend

The leader of the touring boxing group. He used to be a challenger for the Japanese featherweight title. He later became the only person who understands Joe within the touring boxing group. 

He urged Joe to go back to Danpei and his friends and to try to get back into the boxing world. He convinces Joe who then leaves the match that they are having. The people watching the match then gets really angry but inaba and the other boxers start fighting them and they make them say ''Banzai!'' to Joe before he leaves.

Tiger Ozaki is the Bantamweight Japanese National Boxing Champion.

The Japanese Boxing Commision's heads covertly organized a match between Joe and Tiger without the knowledge of Danpei as a way to crush the up and coming Japanese boxer, believing that giving Joe the title shot early in his career would be too much too soon putting a halt to his momentum.

Tiger is first physically seen when Joe Yabuki is invited to train at the Daito Club Boxing Gym. He and his team set up a camera to record Joe's sparring matches there to prepare for their upcoming match with the rising bantamweight star. Joe notices this upon walking into the gym and immediately takes out all of his sparring partners quickly, even fouling the final one. Joe, upset about being spied on then rushes up stairs to the mezzanine to fight Tiger then and there. They are both held back by their trainers and Tiger leaves just as a brawl breaks out between Joe and the Daito Club boxers.

~!In his bout with Joe, Tiger starts off getting the better of Joe by cleanly parrying Yabuki's body blows and countering with punches of his own. Towards the end of the round he is knocked down after biting on an apparent feint upstairs from Joe, before being hit by a crushing shot to the solar plexus, sending the Japanese Champ crashing down to the canvas.!~

~!Tiger then wins all the remaining rounds, him and his team figuring out that Joe is unable to throw a significant punch at his head. Tiger wins by TKO in round 6 when Joe's team throws in the towel. He is next seen in Ryu Harajima's corner during Harajima's fight with Yabuki, instructing him on how to easily beat Joe.!~

~!Tiger's next appearance is in his match against Carlos Rivera, the fighter ranked 6th in the world. Tiger expects an easy fight, thinking that Carlos' wins against the #1 and #2 ranked Japanese fighters were flukes, won only by lucky punches. He is then proved wrong, with Carlos skillfully knocking him out 14 seconds into the first round with an uppercut followed by a hidden elbow strike. This is the last Tiger is seen in both the anime and manga.!~
A printing press worker who seeks out boxing training from Danpei and Joe after being inspired by Joe's matches.

Chibi is part of the kids gang that follows Joe around. Chibi is often forgotten due to how he has very few lines despite appearing throughout the manga. 
He is also rarely shown in the anime and only appears in the very first episodes of the kids gang. 

He has 2 cameos in Ashita no Joe 2, he first appears when he receives a present from Carlos when he's dressed as santa. His second appearance is in episode 43 when he's shown very briefly in the background of the flashback when Joe met Danpei for the first time.
He is the 2nd ranked bantamweight boxer in Japan.

He was one of the prisoners at the Juvenile detention center. He used to be the leader of the sixth dormitory until Joe arrived. 
He came to see Joe's match with Jose Mendoza.

He was one of the prisoners in the sixth dormitory. He went to the Juvenile detention center due to his parents who kept getting complaints about him peering into the girls bath. He came to see the match between Joe and Jose Mendoza.

Oigawa is an anime original character. 

The first time he appears he asks Noriko where Joe's changing room is and he goes to Joe and checks on him without his consent. 
Later on he builds a hut across the river of Danpei's hut and he joins the gym as the gym's doctor.

Inagaki was the National high-school champ. 

In the anime he decided to spar with Joe because he went into their gym without permission and was being rude, Joe ''lost'' the spar and immediately started disliking Inagaki since he was acting arrogant and was making fun of Joe.

They later meet each other again while Joe was taking the pro-test where Inagaki once again was teasing Joe and acting arrogant. (This is where they meet for the first time in the manga) 

Later on during the test they were picked to spar against each other with the fight being for the most part one-sided on Inagaki's behalf. Joe gets more and more frustrated and later on uses his famous ''no-guard'' stance for the first time which throws Inagaki off guard so he misses. 

Joe then starts to hit Inagaki with all he got until he is hit outside of the ring where Joe then chases after him outside of the ring beating him up so hard that he almost thinks he had killed him.

He is the leader out of a small yakuza group that we see at the start of the series.

__Pilot__: We see him with his yakuza group trying to get their money back from Sachi when Joe then beats them all up and takes Hirata down with a body blow. 
__Anime__: We see him appear with a bunch of yakuza members at a playground after Joe had beaten up some of his men. Joe then fights them all. 
__Manga__: He appears in the group of 3 yakuza members that we see at the very start of the manga.

He looks a bit different in each version:
- In the pilot, he appears with a hat, a jacket over his shoulders, and some kind of ''beating'' stick. 
- In the anime, he's wearing a very yellow jacket, a hat, glasses, and a cigarette in his mouth. 
- In the manga, he appears as a medium-sized guy with sunglasses and something in his mouth.

Harajima Ryuu is the no. 1 boxer in the Japan bantamweight division. He is from the Tenoji Boxing club.
He fought Joe after his match with Tiger Ozaki. 

~!The match with Harajima and Joe ended in round 3 with Joe losing by TKO due to him throwing up.!~ 

After Carlos fought Nangou it was his turn to fight Harajima. The match carried out like a normal boxing match, if not worse. 

~!Season 1 and manga: During the end of round 4 Harajima hears a loud whistle coming from the side of the ring and gets distracted. The one who whistled was Robert Harry, Carlos' manager. Harajima gets distracted and that's when Carlos sneaks in a very powerful punch with an elbow blow that goes unnoticed. The bell then rings straight after. Harajima went back to his corner where his coach then explains the situation and how they're gonna win. Harajima is not responding and that's when the coach realizes that Harajima is unconscious. Fearing a KO loss he explains that he can't carry on the match anymore due to Harajima having foot cramps. Harajima then gets woken up in the dressing room with a bucket of water where he then explains to his coach that the punch Carlos sneaked in must've knocked him out. 

Season 2: We get to see parts of Carlos' and Harajimas match on TV, when then see Carlos hit Harajima after the bell rings. Then we see that Carlos won because Harajima couldn't fight anymore.!~
He is the owner of the Hayashi store and is the father of [Noriko](https://anilist.co/character/59779/Noriko-Hayashi)
She is the mother of Noriko and the wife of Seishichi
He is the referee during Shohei and Joe's sparring match for the boxing license.

One of the referee's that appears throughout Ashita no Joe. 
He is the ''main'' referee in season 1 and appears in almost every match that Joe has while in the manga he appears just for a few matches.

Yasuo is an anime original character. 

Yasuo appears in episode 69 of Ashita no Joe. 

Yasuo wanted to pursue a career in boxing so he moved away from his mother and sister's farm life to a bigger city. His boxing career wasn't going that good and he was running low on cash, so he decided to rob his mother and sisters savings. He wore a mask to protect his face so they wouldn't recognize him but after Joe stops him by repeatedly punching him the mother tells Joe to stop since she recognizes Yasuo. 

She then asks Yasuo ''what son robs their own mother'' and tells Yasuo that if he was low on money he should've just asked and gives him the savings. Yasuo then walks away slowly with the money but then turns around and starts crying and runs to hug his mother.

Yuri's mother is an anime original character.

She appears in episode 69 of Ashita no Joe. 

Yuri's mother owns the farm that Joe gets to stay at. She really misses her son and doesn't like boxing since her son Yasuo, went to a bigger city to pursue a boxing career. She lets Joe live on the farm until his broken leg is healed and she starts to feel like he's part of the family. One day when Joe needs some of his clothes sewn, his boxing gloves fall out of his bag and the mother gets shocked and sad and asks if Joe is a boxer. 

One day Yasuo returns to the farm to steal their money but he wears a mask so she wouldn't recognize him. Joe then tries to stop Yasuo and when he keeps punching him the mother tells Joe to stop since she recognizes that it's her son. She gives Yasuo the money but Yasuo after walking a few steps bursts into tears and runs to his mother and hugs her.

Yuri is an anime original character.

Yuri appears in episode 69 of Ashita no Joe. 

After Joe falls from a cliff and breaks his leg, Yuri finds him and let's him rest up on her and her mother's farm until Joe's leg heals. Joe reminds Yuri a lot of her brother Yasuo, who used to also live on the farm before he pursued a career in boxing. She asks Joe if maybe he could be her new ''brother'' where she then runs away embarrassed.
The announcer that appears in the manga and throughout Season 1 and Season 2

The commentator who appears sometimes in the manga and throughout Season 1 and sometimes Season 2 

Note: The name ''Ishida'' only appears in Season 1
He appears in episode 35 during Nishi's match
Ootaka is the chairman/president of the boxing gym with Wolf Kanagushi.

Pancho Leo is a Filipino bantamweight boxer who fought Rikiishi in Rikiishi's first fight as a bantamweight. 
He's ranked eight in his division and he's also a veteran boxer with a 10 year career.

Rikiishi hit Leo with a very powerful uppercut which knocked Leo out and made him lose with a K.O
